A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DecepGPT and contain readable methods, equations, figures and tables with matching core results. v1 ends after its references despite citing Appendices A-C; v3 includes Appendices A-D. Their inclusion is identifiable added documentation, without establishing when those experiments were conducted.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, cross-domain and cross-cultural results, component ablations, training visualizations and generated-report audits.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and supplies additional baseline comparisons, ablations, cultural analyses and report-quality measurements in its appendices.

M1.justification: The SICS adapter, DMC distillation, report-generation schema and joint objective retain their substantive design. Cross-attention is newly explained in Section 3.3 but already appears in v1's Figure 4. The isolated residual-equation discrepancy appears to be an error, rather than evidence of an implemented algorithm change.

E1.justification: The four deception datasets, tasks and cultural populations are retained. Section 4.1 changes the named emotion-pretraining dataset from MER2023 to MER2024, but both versions cite the same MER2024 publication. The PDFs do not establish whether the represented training data changed or the year was corrected.

E2.justification: v1's T4-Deception evaluation reports only DecepGPT; v3's Table A1 adds LieNet, FacialCueNet and PECL comparisons. Table D1 also introduces report-quality comparisons against GPT-4o, VideoLLaMA2 and Qwen2.5-7B-VL. This substantially expands comparator participation for the dataset and report-generation contributions, while retaining the main classification comparator sets.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces METEOR, ROUGE-L, BERTScore and GPT-4o scoring on a 1-10 scale. Section 4.1 revises the stated pretraining setup from MER2023-pretrained projectors to frozen-backbone alignment on MER2024; this does not establish rerunning experiments. Existing classification folds, training budgets and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds cultural cue, modality-contribution and subject-diversity analyses. Appendix B supplies cross-domain SICS/DMC ablations, and Appendix C extends component and backbone analyses to Bag-of-Lies and MU3D. These provide substantial additional mechanism and robustness evidence beyond v1's displayed analyses and references to absent appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the benchmark results. Figure 7's distributions are retained. The newly disclosed 100-output audit sample is procedural information, not an addition to repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main Tables 2-7 retain their numerical results. New Table A1 reports T4 baseline average accuracies of 50.66 for LieNet, 52.3 for FacialCueNet and 54.44 for PECL, alongside DecepGPT's retained 62.58. Tables B1, C1-C2 and D1 add ablation, backbone and report-quality results; DecepGPT's new BERTScore and GPT-Score are 0.812 and 6.96. Figures A1-A3 add cultural and subject statistics.

T1.justification: Equation 1 changes the residual expression's final additive term from b2 in v1 to W2 in v3, introducing an apparent weight/bias error rather than an equivalent rewrite. Other mathematical changes consolidate or renumber existing expressions; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same three contributions: structured reasoning supervision, T4-Deception and SICS/DMC learning modules. Claims about dataset scale, auditability and in-domain/cross-domain performance retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly explains that textual annotations can omit valid cues, motivating expert checks against original videos. Appendix A links cultural cue differences to modality reliance, and Appendix D interprets linguistic scores as evidence of grounded reasoning. Existing principal interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v3 specifies initialization from separate pretrained backbone weights and freezing during emotion alignment. Section 5.3 first documents random sampling of 100 outputs and sequential, mutually exclusive audit categories. Hardware, fine-tuning hyperparameters and statements about supplementary materials and future release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands discussion of visual, attention, graph and video deception models and affective knowledge transfer, adding five deception references. Section 5.3 adds references on object hallucination evaluation, SelfCheckGPT and MMBench to contextualize auditing. The fundamental research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand related work, clarify SICS and initialization, and explain human auditing. Author affiliations, contribution markers, running headers and terminology are corrected. Appendices gain an explicit organization, while the main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures A1-A3 and Tables A1, B1, C1, C2 and D1, substantially expanding the visual evidence. Tables C1-C2 repeat existing DOLOs results while displaying additional datasets. Main displays are relocated or resized, and Figures 1 and 8 receive wording and formatting revisions without new case outcomes.

improvement.justification: v3 makes previously missing ablation evidence inspectable, adds direct T4-Deception baseline comparisons and report-quality measurements, and documents the human-audit procedure. These improve evidential completeness and transparency. The gains are qualified by underspecified cultural-contribution measurements and report-scoring procedures, plus the newly introduced Equation 1 error. Overall, the supplied evidence supports a limited net improvement.
